scenes.narration_en: On June sixteenth, nineteen seventy-six, ten thousand black students marched in Soweto. They refused to learn in Afrikaans, the language of their oppressors.

scenes.narration_en: The apartheid government had imposed Afrikaans as the language of instruction. Students saw this as another tool of racial domination.

scenes.narration_en: Police officers confronted the marching children. Without warning, they opened fire on the unarmed crowd.
scenes.narration_fr: Des policiers confrontèrent les enfants en marche. Sans prévenir, ils tirèrent sur la foule désarmée.

scenes.narration_en: Thirteen-year-old Hector Pieterson was among the first to fall. A photograph of his dying body became a global symbol of apartheid brutality.

scenes.narration_en: Hundreds of students were killed that day. The official death toll was minimized, but witnesses reported massacres across Soweto.
scenes.narration_fr: Des centaines d'élèves furent tués ce jour-là. Le bilan officiel fut minimisé, mais des témoins rapportèrent des massacres à travers Soweto.

scenes.narration_en: The Soweto uprising ignited months of nationwide protests. The apartheid regime faced the most serious challenge in its history.
scenes.narration_fr: La révolte de Soweto déclencha des mois de protestations nationales. Le régime de l'apartheid fit face au défi le plus sérieux de son histoire.

scenes.narration_en: The massacre transformed international opinion. Western nations could no longer ignore the crimes of the apartheid government.
scenes.narration_fr: Le massacre transforma l'opinion internationale. Les nations occidentales ne purent plus ignorer les crimes du gouvernement de l'apartheid.

scenes.narration_en: Schools were burned, businesses were destroyed, and the economy suffered. The apartheid regime responded with mass arrests and torture.
scenes.narration_fr: Des écoles furent brûlées, des commerces détruits et l'économie pâtit. Le régime de l'apartheid répondit par des arrestations massives et la torture.

scenes.narration_en: The Soweto generation became the vanguard of the liberation struggle. Many future leaders of democratic South Africa were forged in those streets.
scenes.narration_fr: La génération de Soweto devint l'avant-garde de la lutte de libération. Beaucoup de futurs dirigeants de l'Afrique du Sud démocratique furent forgés dans ces rues.

scenes.narration_en: June sixteenth is now celebrated as Youth Day in South Africa. It honors the children who gave their lives for freedom and equality.
scenes.narration_fr: Le 16 juin est aujourd'hui célébré comme la Journée de la Jeunesse en Afrique du Sud. Il honore les enfants qui donnèrent leur vie pour la liberté et l'égalité.

scenes.narration_en: Soweto reminds us that youth can change history. Their courage toppled one of the most brutal regimes of the twentieth century.
scenes.narration_fr: Soweto nous rappelle que la jeunesse peut changer l'histoire. Leur courage renversa l'un des régimes les plus brutaux du vingtième siècle.

subjects.summary_en:
In nineteen nineteen, British colonial troops opened fire on unarmed civilians in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar. 
Thousands had gathered to celebrate the Sikh festival of Baisakhi and to protest the repressive Rowlatt Acts. 
General Reginald Dyer arrived with armed soldiers and blocked the only exit without warning the crowd to disperse. 
He ordered his troops to fire directly into the dense gathering of men, women, and children. 
They fired for ten minutes until their ammunition was exhausted, killing hundreds and wounding over a thousand. 
Dyer later claimed his aim was to produce a moral effect throughout Punjab and prevent future rebellion. 
The massacre shocked the Indian subcontinent and turned moderate leaders like Gandhi toward complete independence. 
Rabindranath Tagore renounced his British knighthood in protest against the brutality of colonial rule. 
The Hunter Commission condemned Dyer but he was never prosecuted for murder by British authorities. 
For decades, Britain refused to formally apologize for the massacre. 
In twenty nineteen, the British House of Commons finally expressed deep regret but stopped short of a full apology. 
The Jallianwala Bagh memorial stands today as a sacred site of colonial violence and national resistance. 
It reminds us that freedom demands the courage to resist even the most brutal imperial forces. 
The massacre remains one of the darkest chapters of British colonial rule in India.

Il ordonna a ses troupes de tirer directement sur la foule dense composee d hommes, de femmes et d enfants. 
Ils tirerent pendant dix minutes jusqu a epuisement de leurs munitions, tuant des centaines et blessant plus d un millier. 
Dyer declara plus tard que son objectif etait de produire un effet moral dans tout le Punjab et d empecher de futures rebellions. 
Le massacre choqua le sous-continent indien et poussa des leaders moderes comme Gandhi vers l independance totale. 
Rabindranath Tagore renonca a son titre de chevalier britannique pour protester contre la brutalite de la domination coloniale. 
La commission Hunter condamna Dyer mais il ne fut jamais poursuivi pour meurtre par les autorites britanniques. 
Pendant des decennies, la Grande-Bretagne refusa de s excuser formellement pour le massacre. 
En deux mille dix-neuf, la Chambre des communes britannique exprima enfin un profond regret mais s arreta la.

subjects.summary_en: In December nineteen thirty-seven, Japanese forces captured the Chinese capital of Nanjing and carried out weeks of systematic atrocities against civilians and prisoners of war. Hundreds of thousands of Chinese were killed, and tens of thousands of women were raped in what became known as the Rape of Nanjing. Foreign missionaries and diplomats established a safety zone that saved thousands of lives. Japanese military commanders allowed and encouraged the violence. The International Military Tribunal for the Far East later convicted several commanders of war crimes. Japan has never fully acknowledged the scale of the massacre, and the event remains a source of tension in East Asian relations.
subjects.summary_fr: En decembre mille neuf cent trente-sept, les forces japonaises capturerent la capitale chinoise de Nankin et commirent des semaines d atrocites systematiques contre les civils et les prisonniers de guerre. Des centaines de milliers de Chinois furent tues et des dizaines de milliers de femmes violees dans ce qui devint connu comme le Viol de Nankin. Des missionnaires et diplomates etrangeres etablirent une zone de securite qui sauva des milliers de vies. Les commandants militaires japonais permirent et encouragerent la violence. Le tribunal militaire international pour l Extreme-Orient condamna plus tard plusieurs commandants pour crimes de guerre. Le Japon n a jamais pleinement reconnu l ampleur du massacre, et l evenement demeure une source de tension dans les relations de l Asie de l Est.

subjects.summary_en: In May nineteen twenty-one, a white mob attacked and destroyed the prosperous Black neighborhood of Greenwood in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Known as Black Wall Street, Greenwood was one of the wealthiest African American communities in the United States. The mob burned homes, businesses, and churches while killing hundreds of Black residents. The Oklahoma National Guard arrested Black survivors instead of the rioters. For decades, the massacre was suppressed from history books and official records. In two thousand one, a state commission finally acknowledged the massacre and recommended reparations. Today, the Greenwood Rising history center memorializes the victims and the resilience of the Black community.
subjects.summary_fr: En mai mille neuf cent vingt et un, une foule blanche attaqua et detruisit le quartier noir prospere de Greenwood a Tulsa, Oklahoma. Connu sous le nom de Black Wall Street, Greenwood etait l un des quartiers afro-americains les plus riches des Etats-Unis. La foule brula des maisons, des entreprises et des eglises tout en tuant des centaines de residents noirs. La Garde nationale de l Oklahoma arreta les survivants noirs au lieu des emeutiers. Pendant des decennies, le massacre fut occulte des manuels scolaires et des archives officielles. En deux mille un, une commission de l Etat reconnut enfin le massacre et recommanda des reparations. Aujourd hui, le centre historique Greenwood Rising commemore les victimes et la resilience de la communaute noire.

subjects.title_en: Ruben Um Nyobe and the Forgotten UPC Struggle
subjects.summary_en: In 1948, Ruben Um Nyobe co-founded the UPC, demanding Cameroon's independence from French colonial rule. Forced into hiding, he led resistance from the bush. In 1958, he was ambushed and killed by French forces. His body was never returned.
subjects.summary_fr: En 1948, Ruben Um Nyobè cofonde l'UPC qui réclame l'indépendance du Cameroun face à la colonisation française. Contraint à la clandestinité, il dirige la résistance depuis la brousse. En 1958, il est tué en embuscade par les forces françaises. Son corps ne fut jamais rendu.

sources.name: Achille Mbembe — La Naissance du maquis dans le Sud-Cameroun
